extracted.intended_audience: short story writers, anthology editors, literary critics, and readers interested in editorial selection criteria for American short fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and rules for choosing, classifying, and republishing American short stories for an annual 'best of' anthology (covering stories published in American magazines during a defined year). Includes aesthetic standards, eligibility rules, and asterisk-based ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential human qualities / criticism of life
rubrics_metrics.description: I have set myself the task of disengaging the essential human qualities in our contemporary fiction which, when chronicled conscientiously by our literary artists, may fairly be called a criticism of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor privileges stories that render life imaginatively in organic substance and artistic form; the aim is to capture 'the fresh, living current' and the 'psychological and imaginative reality' conferred by American writers rather than adherence to formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: No value to inorganic fiction (organic substance required)
rubrics_metrics.description: No substance is of importance in fiction, unless it is organic substance, that is to say, substance in which the pulse of life is beating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inorganic fiction is considered an abuse; editors should exercise artistic discrimination to prefer stories where the material is alive and organically related to the story's form and theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of substance (first test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first test of a short story ... is to report upon how vitally compelling the writer makes his selected facts or incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substance is achieved by the artist's power of compelling imaginative persuasion which transforms facts or incidents into a living truth; evaluate how persuasively and vitally the writer renders the chosen material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of form (second test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The true artist will seek to shape this living substance into the most beautiful and satisfying form, by skilful selection and arrangement of his materials, and by the most direct and appealing presentation of it in portrayal and characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After substance, assess the skill of selection, arrangement, portrayal and characterization — the story's craftsmanship and aesthetic form that allow the living substance to take rank above other stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asterisk-based classification / ranking system
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are classified into four groups: (1) those failing either test (no asterisk); (2) those surviving either substance or form (one asterisk); (3) those surviving both tests and worthy of a second reading (two asterisks); (4) a small group uniting genuine substance and artistic form with sincerity (three asterisks, Roll of Honor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use no/one/two/three asterisks to indicate degree of success against the substance/form tests; three-asterisk stories are candidates for republication in the volume. Note: some asterisks in the Roll of Honor may indicate the editor's personal preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publication period and source
rubrics_metrics.description: The present record covers the period from October 1920 to September 1921, inclusive. During this period, I have sought to select from the stories published in American magazines those which have rendered life imaginatively in organic substance and artistic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit selection to stories published in the defined period and in American magazines; scope of review is explicitly temporal and source-based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and author-frequency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been a point of honor with me not to republish a story by an English author or by any foreign author. I have also made it a rule not to include more than one story by an individual author in the volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply exclusion of foreign-authored stories for republication and a one-story-per-author cap when assembling the anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering not a judgment of comparative excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The order in which the stories in this volume are printed is not intended as an indication of their comparative excellence; the arrangement is alphabetical by authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange the final selections alphabetically (or otherwise explicitly mark ordering as non-evaluative) to avoid implying a ranked preference among included stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of formulaic/organized criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: I am not at all interested in formulae, and organized criticism at its best would be nothing more than dead criticism, as all dogmatic interpretation of life is always dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor intuitive, living responses to fiction and the story's imaginative reality over rigid formulae or dogmatic critical systems when judging literary merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial impartiality with acknowledged personal preference
rubrics_metrics.description: In compiling these lists I have permitted no personal preference or prejudice to consciously influence my judgment. To the titles of certain stories, however, in the 'Rolls of Honor,' an asterisk is prefixed, and this asterisk, I must confess, reveals in some measure a personal preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for objective selection according to the stated tests, but transparently acknowledge any personal preferences that affect choices; mark such cases if necessary.
